rituals.name: WORD MELT
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Charged → Listen Moment → Return Seen
rituals.recognition_cue: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
rituals.immediate_need: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
rituals.match_reason: Automatic-pattern blindness · Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
rituals.goal: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.
rituals.win: ✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.
rituals.tips:
• Let more control guide the response, even with automatic behaviour present.
• Autopilot can change shape when pressure drops.
• Do not confuse automatic behaviour with a permanent verdict.
• You can honour automatic behaviour and still refuse autopilot.
• Take autopilot seriously without treating it as destiny.

rituals.immediate_need: Competence grows at the edge, not at the cliff.
rituals.match_reason: Shame globalisation · Competence grows at the edge, not at the cliff.

rituals.name: SET THE CONVERSATION SIZE
rituals.unique_game_move: Read Bandwidth → Send Signal → Set Reopen
rituals.recognition_cue: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
rituals.immediate_need: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
rituals.match_reason: Communication distortion · A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
rituals.goal: A conversation can be important and still need a smaller container today.
rituals.steps:
1. Read Bandwidth — Choose your current safe bandwidth: ONE SENTENCE, THREE SENTENCES, or FULL CONVERSATION.
2. Choose Size — Name the purpose that must fit inside that size: acknowledge, request, pause, clarify, or repair.
3. Send Signal — Draft or say only the selected amount. Stop when the sentence limit is reached, even if more remains.
4. Set Reopen — Name when or under what condition the next level can reopen. If you cannot offer one, state that honestly without making a false promise.
rituals.win: ✓ I stated that honestly without making a false promise.
rituals.winReward: ✓ I stated that honestly without making a false promise.
rituals.tips:
• Do not use motive guessing as proof that a difficult conversation is correct.
• Use a specific request to keep communication strain from becoming everything.
• Let understanding grow quietly beside defensiveness.
• Your choice around conflict heat can be simple: a respectful boundary.
• A difficult conversation is real; conflict spreading is still optional.

rituals.name: THEN / NOW SUBTITLES
rituals.unique_game_move: Alternate Lines → Keep Eyes → Date Location
rituals.recognition_cue: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
rituals.immediate_need: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
rituals.match_reason: Memory-as-present confusion · Flashbacks need temporal translation.
rituals.goal: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
rituals.steps:
1. Alternate Lines — When memory body alarm begins, alternate lines: THEN—state one past fact; NOW—state one current difference.
2. Include Age — Include age, place, available help, bodily freedom, and exits.
3. Keep Eyes — Keep eyes open and touch the environment after every pair.
4. Date Location — The screen may replay; the subtitles restore date and location.
rituals.win: ✓ Gave the replay a date and location instead of letting it become now.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Gave the replay a date and location instead of letting it become now.
rituals.tips:
• Make space for distance before asking for certainty.
• Do not abandon distance just because a memory surge is loud.
• Keep responsibility proportionate when a memory surge gets personal.
• Let today's evidence sit beside the memory, not underneath it.
• One dose of a safe current anchor can reopen present safety.

rituals.name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.ritual_name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.unique_game_move: Name Pair → Swap Variable → Tag Driver
rituals.recognition_cue: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.immediate_need: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.match_reason: Emotion blending · Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.goal: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.
rituals.win: ✓ Noticed which emotion moved and which stayed.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Noticed which emotion moved and which stayed.
rituals.tips:
• Let emotional weather be difficult without making peak-intensity deciding necessary.
• Keep clarity visible when a strong feeling gets loud.
• Pause emotional obedience; give a wider view a fair chance.
• Let perspective have more influence than mood evidence today.
• Choose a wider view; you can reassess after emotional weather softens.

rituals.name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
rituals.unique_game_move: Pin Forecast → Score Odds → Update Odds
rituals.recognition_cue: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.immediate_need: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.match_reason: Probability overestimation · A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.steps:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.
rituals.win: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
rituals.tips:
• Let realism remain possible even if catastrophic thinking stays.
• Fear’s loudest ending is real; coping discounting is still optional.
• Do not abandon a workable plan just because fear’s loudest ending is loud.
• Give actual probabilities a turn before repeating certainty inflation.
• Let a disaster prediction be difficult without making coping discounting necessary.

rituals.name: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.unique_game_move: Read Channels → Move Dial → Check Panel
rituals.recognition_cue: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
rituals.immediate_need: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
rituals.match_reason: Body alarm escalation · The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
rituals.goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
rituals.steps:
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.
rituals.win: ✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.
rituals.tips:
• Let settling grow quietly beside a surge of fear.
• Take slower breathing seriously when panic feels overwhelming.
• Keep a little space steady while panic moves through.
• Do not turn panic into a reason for catastrophe checking.
• You can respect a racing sensation without obeying body scanning.

rituals.name: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
rituals.unique_game_move: Run Pulse → Read Strain → Set Gear
rituals.recognition_cue: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
rituals.immediate_need: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
rituals.match_reason: Action avoidance · Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
rituals.goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
rituals.steps:
1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
rituals.win: ✓ One work pulse found the gear motivation could only guess at.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One work pulse found the gear motivation could only guess at.

• Make space for forward motion before asking for certainty.
• When avoidance rises, return to one doable move.
• Choose a smaller beginning before deciding that starting pressure will last.
• Before reacting to avoidance, ask what protects momentum.
• Let traction set the direction when starting pressure feels loud.

rituals.ritual_name: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
rituals.unique_game_move: State Clearly → Name Boundary → Let Value
rituals.recognition_cue: Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.
rituals.immediate_need: Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.
rituals.match_reason: Boundary confusion · Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.
rituals.goal: Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.
rituals.steps:
1. State Clearly — State clearly what was wrong or unwanted.
2. Name Boundary — Then name one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value you can carry forward without claiming the event was beneficial.
3. Let Value — Let the value belong to you, not to the harm.
rituals.win: ✓ The load shrank to the piece that truly belongs here.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The load shrank to the piece that truly belongs here.
rituals.tips:

• Do not turn over-responsibility into a reason for boundary guilt.
• Do not let over-responsibility decide what you deserve.
• Your responsibility has edges; guilt does not erase them.
• Give a respectful no a turn before repeating rescuing.

rituals.name: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Skill → Demote Voice → Finish Unit
rituals.recognition_cue: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
rituals.immediate_need: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
rituals.match_reason: Tunnel vision · Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
rituals.goal: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Centre Feedback — Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.

• Use one clear priority to stay connected with focus.
• Choose what supports a quieter mind, not what feeds multitasking.

rituals.name: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
rituals.unique_game_move: State Rule → Compare Effects → Keep Core
rituals.recognition_cue: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
rituals.immediate_need: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
rituals.match_reason: Context neglect · A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
rituals.goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
rituals.steps:
1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.
rituals.win: ✓ The rule kept its ethical core and lost its fake universality.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The rule kept its ethical core and lost its fake universality.
rituals.tips:
• Pause confirmation seeking; give contrary evidence a fair chance.
• Before reacting to one-sided evidence, ask what protects perspective.
• Let accuracy survive the pull toward confirmation seeking.
• Use the full picture to make a narrowed conclusion more manageable.
• Do not use one-sided certainty as proof that one-sided evidence is correct.

rituals.name: CHANGE THE COMPARISON DENOMINATOR
rituals.unique_game_move: Name Mind → Compare Progress → Group Exists
rituals.recognition_cue: A distorted reference group can manufacture failure.
rituals.immediate_need: A distorted reference group can manufacture failure.
rituals.match_reason: Comparison distortion · A distorted reference group can manufacture failure.
rituals.goal: A distorted reference group can manufacture failure.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Mind — Name the group your mind selected.
2. Match Resources — Substitute a baseline matched on starting point, resources, time, responsibilities, and opportunity.
3. Compare Progress — Compare progress with context included.
4. Group Exists — If no fair group exists, use your own prior trajectory.
rituals.win: ✓ The comparison group lost power; my own trajectory became the ruler.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The comparison group lost power; my own trajectory became the ruler.
rituals.tips:
• Use your actual values when comparison starts narrowing your options.
• You can honour social ranking and still refuse scorekeeping.
• Make space for self-worth before asking for certainty.
• Choose a fairer comparison because belonging deserves protection.
• One dose of one self-respecting choice can reopen perspective.
